A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with complete, readable main text and Appendices A–W. Text comparison and page rendering support reliable comparison of equations, algorithms, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original compressed-sensing and sparse-regression experiments in Section 5, plus appendix experiments on correlated features, gradient pursuit, column subset selection, and complex signals.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experimental results in Section 5 and the appendices, including recovery rates, reconstruction errors, regression scores, and runtime comparisons.

M1.justification: Appendix E.3, Algorithm 4 corrects OP-Splicing: ξ_j changes from criterion (8) to (10), ζ_j from (10) to (8), and the removal-set comparison changes from ξ_j ≥ ξ_i to ξ_j ≤ ξ_i. These revise the documented scoring and removal procedure to match the existing criteria; no new component is introduced.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic recovery scenarios, AudioSet signals, six regression datasets, grayscale images for column subset selection, and complex-signal estimation scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged, including OMP, CoSaMP, and (A)BESS in the corresponding experiments, Gradient Pursuit in Appendix U, and the SVD-128/SVD-256 leverage-score baselines in Table 3.

E3.justification: Data dimensions, preprocessing, sampling rates, noise settings, metrics, and Appendix R's five-fold cross-validation protocol are unchanged. The pseudocode corrections do not establish revised experimental settings or reruns.

E4.justification: The correlated-feature robustness experiments in Appendix P, CoSaMP failure analysis in Appendix Q, and convergence/runtime analyses in Appendix U are retained without changes.

E5.justification: Both report 500 independent synthetic recovery runs, 100 AudioSet experiments, and the same mean/standard-deviation reporting in Table 1. Runtime repetition counts and statistical reporting practices are also unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical tables, experimental plots, rankings, and reported findings are unchanged, including Table 1, Table 3, and the appendix results. No results are added, removed, or revised alongside the algorithm correction.

T1.justification: The selection/elimination definitions, optimality and convergence statements, assumptions, and appendix proofs are unchanged. Algorithm 4 corrects how existing criteria are applied without revising their mathematical derivation or theoretical guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about optimal selection/elimination criteria, meta-substitution, preserved theoretical properties, and empirical gains at the same computational complexity order.

C2.justification: Explanations of feature interactions, correlated-feature advantages, CoSaMP failures, computational costs, applicability, and future extensions are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices.

D1.justification: Algorithm 4 provides corrected implementation instructions for assigning selection/elimination scores and ranking removal candidates, improving reproducibility of OP-Splicing. Other technical details and code/data access information are unchanged; changes to executed code are not established.

R1.justification: The references and research positioning are identical, including Remark 3.8's relationship to Tohidi et al. and the stated distinction between their approach and this paper's framework.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v2 dated 30 May 2025 to v3 dated 15 August 2025. Prose, terminology, headings, and document organization are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, captions, styling, and placement are unchanged. Algorithm 4's corrections occur within the existing display without restructuring or reflowing the page.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects two operational inconsistencies in Algorithm 4: reversed criterion assignments and the wrong elimination ranking. This aligns the pseudocode with the existing selection/elimination theory and reduces the risk of incorrect implementation. The benefit is limited but concrete; the scientific claims, proofs, and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
